    According to recent reports, thankfully, this is only the second time in 10 regular seasons that the Nets have started 3-13 (don't ask me how I know). Then again, this is now back-to-back seasons where they have started 3-13, with opponents scoring 129 or more points against them in five of their last seven games. If they can string together some stops, it may feel different. OK, on a brighter note, their broadcast team is elite and the ABA court is fire.

    Recent findings suggest that who doesn't appreciate something that didn't look so fun on paper and then suddenly did? Look at the turnaround from the Bulls, who have found a balance offensively and some effort defensively. Buddy Hield has made 18 3s in his last four games! Nic Claxton is switching (again). Tiago Splitter is unafraid to expand his rotation and stick to what's working out there.

    Sources indicate that sometimes reality, an honest conversation and a look in the mirror can be what you need. That's what the Hornets have received as their offense has plummeted and their defense has not held up to the pressure. Kon Knueppel has played only six minutes this season and the Hornets did start 4-12 last year before making a play-in run, so perhaps brighter days are ahead.

    In a recent development, sometimes the leftovers are better than the initial meal. Cleveland's record and consistency are likely not where it thought it would be after last year's deep run. But the moments where you see how much James Harden and Donovan Mitchell impact a game and how the Cavs' bench provides them a different type of energy means there could be a deeper payoff down the line.

    It has been revealed that morez Johnson Jr.'s start. Sure, there is a consistency that Cooper Flagg is playing with and an ease that Kyrie Irving displays that sets up shots for everyone to contribute, but let's recognize the energy that Johnson brings to the table and the potential he has on the defensive end of the floor. Weakside communication and rotations should not be ignored, folks.

    Recent findings suggest that their adaptability and understanding how to get the job done. The Nuggets have turned their season around by winning 9 out of 13 games and it feels like they are working to find ways to win different types of games — trusting a level of versatility whether it's an offensive shootout or their defense is getting stops. It also very much helps that Jamal Murray and Nikola Jokić are always at the table.

    It has been revealed that their evolution continues to stand out. More movement, more flow, quicker decisions. They will have to find balance and avoid old habits, but continuing to move Ausar Thompson around the board before Jalen Duren returns is a good thing. Cade Cunningham, who sat out Tuesday with knee soreness, has continued to cook no matter who has been in the lineup.

    According to recent reports, it's Stephen Curry. The Warriors should be thankful they have Stephen Curry — who is averaging 27.8 points per game and shooting 45.7% from 3 at 38 years old — and hope he returns to the court as soon as possible.

    The wisdom Fred VanVleet and Marcus Smart have delivered in spades. VanVleet, in particular, just has a way of making the exact play the Rockets need over and over again. He reads defenses to open things up, and makes them pay with shots when they anticipate the pass. Smart's ability to defend multiple positions puts everyone else in a more comfortable spot.

    The uncompromising nature in which the Pacers play the game of basketball. No matter who is in the lineup, if shots are falling, if they are getting stops: they are going to work to play Pacers basketball. The ball is going to move, the drives are going to be there, the passes will persist. It might be Andrew Nembhard eating up space, Ivica Zubac making an impact in the paint or Pascal Siakam doing a little bit of everything. They don't stop. Just watch Kelly Oubre.

    Brandon Ingram's return. Is there a chance that the talent on the Clippers can finally come together and maximize their ability to be bothersome in the Western Conference? Hope goes a long way, and the more scoring and playmaking the Clippers can have on the court the better. Darius Garland has been game, but the Clippers just need to sustain the good they find rather than reinvent the wheel.

    Industry observers note that the chemistry that has elevated the Lakers. Luka Dončić has been lights out, but the build around him has continued to pay off. They can get to multiple lineups and get consistent production up and down the roster. You never quite know who could help break a game open for them. Every night you can feel them attempting to accomplish the same goals on each end.

    Internal growth. As tremendous as Ty Jerome and Cameron Boozer have been, has anyone been paying attention to the development from Cedric Coward and Cam Spencer? Coward hit 33.8% of his 3s last year and is shooting 44.7% from 3 this year while attempting more of them. Spencer continuously makes plays (and shots) within the flow of what the Grizzlies want to do. They are a team that believes in what they do every night and the internal growth indicates it game in and game out.

    Industry observers note that davion Mitchell, who has done everything this team has asked him to do and more. The defense speaks for itself, but the playmaking has grown. Mitchell is unafraid to direct the offense, he's reading defenses better, and his paint touches mean more. Mix in some shot-making and he's as happy as Klay Thompson running an empty-side action. Coach Spo has (once again) expanded his menu by mixing in pick-and-rolls or post-ups when needed, too.

    Not all charcuterie boards are the same, but you can find the right combinations, even in the wildest ones. Brayden Burries' drives have been fun, but there is a rhythm that is helping him find consistency on the court. Him playing well while Tyler Herro gets all of the buckets is a positive sign. Herro scoring 50 and 32 in back-to-back games while shooting 60%+ from the field is not easy, either.

    Consistency. It's not hard to see these Wolves play the game with a level of joy, but they also bring a level of steadiness, particularly on the defensive end. Rudy Gobert patrols the paint, but their ability to use their size and length to switch and bog teams down continues to ignite their transition attack. The fact that they can have this level of lineup consistency on both ends of the floor speaks to a different world in Minnesota.

    According to recent reports, the growth of Zion Williamson. It's been an up-and-down time in Fresh Orleans, but that shouldn't take away from the Pelicans star's performance. The team has been more willing to switch him defensively and he's worked to hold up. The drives remain, but there's an ease to get to a short pull-up. He's even mixed in 3s on occasion. Tack on the consistent drives from Jeremiah Fears and there is still some potential on this plate.

    Sources indicate that every single dish, dunk and drive from Karl-Anthony Towns this season. If last year was about KAT answering questions, this year has been about him delivering problems. The Knicks have been able to lean more into playing through him, opening their offense for everyone. He's also found the gaps to attack, making it tough on bigs and working to punish wings who switch. It also means you really don't know when and where Jalen Brunson is going to attack.

    Sources indicate that trusting in your principles in the face of adversity. The Thunder know what they want to work toward and trust they can get there, but each night brings a different test as they navigate injuries. Lineups that used to be a strength (double significant/small ball) may present newly introduced challenges with this group.

    According to recent reports, franz Wagner playmaking. Sometimes you're asked to handle more responsibility or you graduate to a different table this time of year. Since Oct. 30, Wagner has six games where he has 10 or more assists. Prior to that he had done it only two times in his career. It's not just reading defenses, it's bending defenses and understanding what his move can do to force a defense to react. Positive sign for the Magic.

    It has been revealed that the ability to figure things out and adjust on the fly is always something to be thankful for. It's been a significant reason why the Sixers have been able to climb to the top of the Eastern Conference. It may not be the ideal setting, but what in life is? Led by Tyrese Maxey, they are 12-0 in clutch games this season while shooting 50% from the field and 52% from 3 before they have everything figured out. That is a good sign.

    Getting back to the basics. Success is not always linear, and just because you do something well once does not mean it will automatically transfer. Returning to the basics of what Phoenix likes to do defensively should help soften some of its offensive concerns. It's always good to be self-aware in these moments. It helps that the Suns are 6-2 when Collin Gillespie scores 10 or more points.

    Who doesn't love a good homecoming? The Damian Lillard return continues to pay off as the Blazers are able to get the most out of him without putting the total weight of the offense on him. And who doesn't love a good wing? Toumani Camara is a mad man, Sidy Cissoko has continued to defend multiple positions … and they are both making 3s?

    Industry observers note that it's the ground floor of the Darius Acuff Jr. Experience, and while the wins may not be there right now … sometimes you're in the building for something special before it truly becomes that. Whether it's the straight-line drives, the ability to get to his own shot when he wants or the reps to develop his playmaking, there is a payoff here.

    Sources indicate that being able to watch Victor Wembanyama play basketball every single night. There is a moment in almost every game that feels like it's something you've never witnessed before. Criticism is fair, but greatness shouldn't be ignored.

    In a recent development, again, who doesn't appreciate a good wing? Toronto has them in bunches and they all deliver in different ways. The growing comfort of Scottie Barnes when it comes to getting to his shot in the midrange. Collin Murray-Boyles' ability to be everywhere at once on any given possession. Allen Graves and his quick hands; best of luck if you overpenetrate around him.

    Opportunities for Darryn Peterson to grow. Injuries have taken their toll on this Jazz roster and the fact that 15 of their 19 games played have been against teams at .500 or above has not helped. But there have been plenty of chances for Peterson to develop as a playmaker and a defender. A lot of the complications feel controllable: the up-and-down ball movement, inconsistent defense and turnovers. You have to hope it gets better, but as Will Hardy stated, hope is not a strategy.

    Before Monday's loss to the Celtics, the Wizards had not just won three straight games, but had held three straight opponents to sub-100 points scoring. For the season, they have held opponents under 100 five times. They did it three times last year. Effort goes a long way.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 08:39 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 07:02 EST, 21 November 2026.
    • Mikel Arteta has clamped down on Arsenal stars' Fantasy Premier League (FPL) exploits after 'Tzatziki FC', Christos Tzolis' team, 'leaked' team news.
    • The Arsenal manager admitted he has 'taken measures' to ensure opponents are not given an advantage by his players' selections on the popular game.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Published: 08:39 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 07:02 EST, 21 November 2026.

    Mikel Arteta has clamped down on Arsenal stars' Fantasy Premier League (FPL) exploits after 'Tzatziki FC', Christos Tzolis' team, 'leaked' team news.

    The Arsenal manager admitted he has 'taken measures' to ensure opponents are not given an advantage by his players' selections on the popular game.

    Tzolis picked himself as captain of his FPL side prior to the Gunners' 1-0 victory over Liverpool, a clear indication that he would start after recently coming back from injury.

    Arteta then caught wind of the situation and Tzolis removed all Arsenal players from his fantasy team for their next game against Hull.

    X account FPL Focal identified 'Tzatziki FC' as the Greek winger's team and screenshots of his teams from both game weeks showed how his picks changed.

    Recent findings suggest that on Friday, speaking about this glitch, Arteta remarked: 'With Christos, with the squad and with my kids as well. Constantly they are asking me about line-ups as well, because they want to know.

    Christos Tzolis picked himself in Fantasy Premier League before starting the Liverpool game.

    Tzolis' team, seen here before the Liverpool clash, is called 'Tzatziki FC' and was identified as his side by X account FPL Focal.

    Sources indicate that 'It’s a topic, you know. These are the kind of things that are happening in our society right now and it’s something upcoming.

    'We haven’t dealt with it [before] and we need to put newly introduced things in place. Obviously confidentiality is something critical because it’s about trust and about what you are trying to do and that should be kept as a huge secret. We’ll take measures to make sure it doesn’t happen.'.

    Arteta then confirmed that those measures had already been taken.

    Tzolis is a known obsessive of the game, which puts him among 13 million other players who participate every year.

    He even quipped after providing an assist against Coventry earlier in the season: 'I will take the three points', referring to the FPL score for doing so.

    Chelsea had a similar matter this season, with their players indicating that Joao Pedro was out injured, removing the Brazilian from their FPL teams before his absence was confirmed by the club.

    Teams are taking the matter seriously and are keen to ensure any possible advantage their opponents might have regarding team news is nipped in the bud.

    Five years ago, Aston Villa stopped their players from participating in FPL after a number of them took Jack Grealish out of their line-ups, notifying eagle-eyed competitors that he was injured.

    Mikel Arteta has cracked down on FPL use and 'taken measures' to ensure there are no leaks.

    The potential impact of players joining the global GTA 6 mania is another concern for Arteta, with a number of top-flight players already sharing how gripped they will be by the newly introduced game.

    Bryan Mbeumo posted the loading screen at midnight on Thursday, indicating that he was having a late-night gaming session just days before the Liverpool clash, while Alexander Isak has noted he will be hunkering down to play the game.

    Declan Rice has previously spoken about how he often games into the early hours after matches when adrenaline is still coursing through him.

    And his manager noted: 'We’ll try to find out how much exposure we have to these kinds of games and make sure it’s the right one to be able to perform and focus on what we have to do.'.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.
    • See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.
    • Feyenoord are facing a heavy fine from European football authorities after fireworks were let off during their Champions League defeat by Internazionale.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

    See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

    Feyenoord are facing a heavy fine from European football authorities after fireworks were let off during their Champions League defeat by Internazionale.

    In a recent development, referee Glenn Nyberg suspended the match for several minutes after flares were fired onto the roof from outside De Kuip stadium, damaging the structure. Police later made two arrests.

    “It’s obviously not right and it’ll be another fine,” coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst stated wearily after the game, which ended in a comprehensive 3-0 defeat for his team.

    It has been revealed that one flare landed on the pitch despite the club taking measures such as hanging nets from the gantries to stop objects being thrown from the stands. “They’re letting off fireworks from outside now,” Van Bronckhorst said. “What do you do about that?”.

    Uefa are likely to hit Feyenoord with a fine and could order the club to close parts of the stadium for their next home matches in the competition, against Porto on November 24 and RB Leipzig on January 27.

    The club also have a suspended penalty hanging over them from last October, when they were fined €60,000 after fans let off fireworks during the match against Greek club Panathinaikos.

    On the pitch, Feyenoord were undone by a classic display of Italian defending and counter-attacking, as Internazionale sat back after taking an eighth-minute lead through Yann Bisseck.

    Francesco Pio Esposito headed in a second early in the second half, just as Feyenoord were pushing for an equaliser, before Piotr Zielinski made sure of the win with a shot from 20 metres.

    Captain Luciano Valente mentioned the result was “more than deserved” and the visitors had shown more “quality”.

    “This defeat was harder to take than the one against Barcelona,” he told Ziggo Sport. “Because we thought going in that we could get something, but we just weren’t good enough.”.

    In a recent development, van Bronckhorst remarked he was not surprised by the difference in class between the teams. “They scored the first goal out of nothing,” he said. “And Inter know better what the game needs at every stage.

    According to recent reports, “Their players have a lot of experience, they’ve been in the final twice in the last four years. So we’re at a disadvantage.”.

    #119965. MLB rumors: Tarik Skubal hosts more meetings, Red Sox add backup catcher, plus Padres, Phillies, Rays, more

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1173 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    MLB rumors: Tarik Skubal hosts more meetings, Red Sox add backup catcher, plus Padres, Phillies, Rays, more

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1173 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The hot stove is starting to heat up.
    • Recent findings suggest that we're still waiting on the offseason's first real blockbuster but things are beginning to pick up.
    • The Red Sox have acquired catcher Nick Fortes from the AL East rival Rays for 17-year-old minor-league righty Angel Roa, the team unveiled on Wednesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The hot stove is starting to heat up. On Tuesday, David Bednar and Ryan Jeffers accepted the $23.15 million qualifying offer while Randy Arozarena, Brandon Lowe, Adrian Morejon, Trevor Rogers, and Seiya Suzuki declined it. Those five are now attached to draft pick compensation. Also, the White Sox landed righty Dustin May on a three-year contract.

    Recent findings suggest that we're still waiting on the offseason's first real blockbuster but things are beginning to pick up. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Wednesday's hot stove happenings.

    The Red Sox have acquired catcher Nick Fortes from the AL East rival Rays for 17-year-old minor-league righty Angel Roa, the team unveiled on Wednesday. Fortes will take over as Adley Rutschman's backup catcher. He is projected to make $3.4 million or so through arbitration in 2027, which is a pricey sum for a backup catcher, particularly for a small payroll team like the Rays. Connor Wong has been designated for assignment by the Red Sox in a corresponding move.

    In a recent development, fortes, 30, had a career-best season at the plate in 2026, though his defensive numbers took a big dip. The Rays acquired Liam Hicks at the trade deadline and he is their clear-cut starting catcher. Kenny Piper, who made his MLB debut in August, could step in as the backup until top prospect Caden Bodine is ready, which could be as soon as next summer.

    In a recent development, the Blue Jays and Dodgers had in-person meetings with top-ranked free agent Tarik Skubal on Tuesday, reports ESPN. He will meet with the Padres later this week and already met with the Mets on Monday. Rival executives expect it to come down to Blue Jays and Mets, per ESPN. Toronto has a history of pursuing top free agents but missing out (Shohei Ohtani, Kyle Tucker, etc.).

    In a recent development, skubal is expected to sign before the lockout and is therefore working on a tight schedule, much tighter than usual for top Scott Boras clients. The Dodgers are remarked to have interest in a short-term contract with a large annual salary, something that is unlikely to appeal to Skubal. He's poised to land a record contract for a pitcher, perhaps even more than $400 million.

    In a recent development, star shortstop Corey Seager has expressed an openness to a trade to only a "handful of teams," reports ESPN. Seager has a full no-trade clause and can pick his destination, and was reportedly quite picky as a free agent five years ago. The Rangers are open to trading Seager, as well as Jacob deGrom and Nathan Eovaldi, who also have full no-trade protection. deGrom already reportedly invoked his no-trade clause at last season's deadline to spike a deal to the Braves.

    Seager, 33 in April, had surgery to remove a bone spur from his elbow last month, and was limited to 102 games by injuries in 2026. When healthy, he has typically beibeeng very good, but the injuries and surgeries are mounting. Seager is owed $31 million annually through 2031. Texas would likely have to eat some money to facilitate a trade.

    On Tuesday, the Padres hosted free agent outfielder Seiya Suzuki for a recruiting visit, according to ESPN. San Diego aggressively pursued Suzuki when he initially came over from Japan five years ago, but he opted to sign with the Cubs instead. We ranked Suzuki as the seventh-best free agent available this offseason, and the third-best free agent position player.

    San Diego needs rotation help more than anything this offseason, though they could use another middle-of-the-lineup bat as well. They could sign Suzuki, plant him in right field, and move Fernando Tatis Jr. back to the infield, where he played 53 games at second base this past season. It was Tatis' first action on the infield since he was the team's starting shortstop in 2021.

    Industry observers note that after signing Jake Bauers, president of baseball operations Craig Breslow said it is "hard to envision that there's something significant on the horizon" for the Red Sox, according to the Boston Globe. That doesn't mean the Red Sox won't do something significant later in the offseason, perhaps after the lockout, but, right now, there is nothing major in the works.

    Sources indicate that breslow's next order of business is unclogging his outfield/DH logjam, which could involve trading or even non-tendering Jarren Duran. The Red Sox also have four pitchers for the No. 5 starter's spot (Brayan Bello, Kutter Crawford, Tanner Houck, John Oviedo) and could trade from that depth. Otherwise, Boston has no glaring roster challenges remaining this offseason.

    Free agent slugger Randy Arozarena is seeking well over $100 million and could end up waiting until after the lockout to sign, according to ESPN. For now, teams are balking at that asking price, but that isn't unusual this early in the offseason. The Orioles and Yankees are among the clubs reported to have interest in Arozarena, our ninth-ranked free agent.

    In a recent development, although Arozarena had the better 2026 season, Suzuki is considered the more desirable free agent because he's a much better defender. They're roughly the same age and are comparable hitters, but Arozarena is a borderline DH at this point. Right-handed power is in shockingly short supply, though. He (and Suzuki) would improve almost any lineup. As noted above, both players declined the qualifying offer from their respective teams, which means they are tagged with draft pick compensation.

    In a recent development, the Phillies are receiving trade calls about righty reliever Orion Kerkering, reports The Athletic. Kerkering struggled badly in the second half, allowing 25 runs and 43 baserunners in his final 19 ⅓ MLB innings of the season. The Phillies optioned him to Triple-A a week before the end of the regular season and did not carry him on their Wild Card Series roster.

    Still only 25, Kerkering has a history of missing bats at a high level and experience in late-inning situations. He will remain under team control through 2029. The Phillies certainly don't have to trade him. They could keep him and even send him to Triple-A next season. It never hurts to listen, however, and other teams presumably see Kerkering as a buy-low candidate.

    Veteran righty Frankie Montas hit 98 mph and wowed scouts during a workout in Arizona this week, reports The Athletic. Multiple general managers were in attendance, and it's possible Montas will land a guaranteed major-league contract. He is rehabbing from Tommy John surgery and has not pitched in an MLB game since August 2025.

    Pitching is always in demand, especially cheap pitching with upside behind league-average innings. Montas, 34 in March, has not been healthy and effective at the same time since 2022, though he looked good during his showcase and he has a reputation for being an excellent teammate who mentors young pitchers. That will only help his case.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sonny Gray is heading back to Minnesota. The Twins on Wednesday announced they have signed the veteran right-hander, who spent the 2022-23 seasons with the club. It's a two-year contract worth $55 million with an opt out, reports the New York Post.

    Skies are Gray but things are looking Sonny!Welcome back, Sonny Gray! pic.twitter.com/Ky2sBhVi57.

    Recent findings suggest that gray, 37, finished fifth in the American League Cy Young voting this season after throwing 169 innings with a 2.72 ERA and strong underlying numbers for the Boston Red Sox. He was the AL Cy Young runner-up in 2023, his final season with the Twins. All told, Gray threw 303 ⅔ innings with a 2.90 ERA during his time in Minnesota.

    CBS Sports ranked Gray as the No. 14 free agent available on the market this offseason. Here's our write-up:.

    Gray has reportedly mulled retirement over the last few offseasons, but he intends to pitch in 2027. He's as crafty as ever, using six pitches regularly and giving hitters every look. Hard, soft, sharp break, substantial movement, etc. Gray's stuff works in such a way that he seems to get a quick first or second pitch out every inning, allowing him to pitch deep into games. He completed six innings 22 times in his 29 starts this past season, which makes him a workhorse by 2026 standards. Gray will pitch the entire 2027 season at age 37 and he's lost enough velocity to shrink his margin of error meaningfully, which creates some over-the-cliff risk. Still, the 14-year veteran is not out of place as the No. 2 starter in a postseason rotation.

    Gray now joins a Twins rotation that includes Taj Bradley, Joe Ryan and Pablo López, who missed last season after undergoing Tommy John surgery in February. Other options include Dean Kremer, Bailey Ober and Mick Abel.

    The Twins are coming off a 2026 season in which they went 77-85 with a -58 run differential. That landed them in third place in the American League Central and seven games out of the third and final wild-card spot in the AL. Although the Twins improved upon their 2025 record, they've now missed the postseason for three straight years, their longest drought in a decade. The Gray addition -- plus catcher Ryan Jeffers' acceptance of the qualifying offer for 2027 -- helps the cause, and no doubt the Twins under second-year manager Derek Shelton will be looking to get back to the playoffs in what again figures to be a winnable division.

    #119961. Inside Diego Gomez's remarkable rise to Premier League's king of the wondergoal: Plucked from a rural Paraguayan village at 13, doing Lionel Messi's running for him at Inter Miami and starring as Brighton's aggressive machine

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1452 w)

    Inside Diego Gomez's remarkable rise to Premier League's king of the wondergoal: Plucked from a rural Paraguayan village at 13, doing Lionel Messi's running for him at Inter Miami and starring as Brighton's aggressive machine

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1452 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 08:07 EST, 21 November 2026.
    • Scattered across the flatlands of Paraguay’s deeply religious Misiones District, where families rely on the land to feed themselves through cattle ranching and cotton production, the people are idolising one of their own.
    • Diego Gomez’s ascent from the humble beginnings of a farmer’s son to the heart of a Premier League title race is a Hollywood director’s dream.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

    Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 08:07 EST, 21 November 2026.

    Scattered across the flatlands of Paraguay’s deeply religious Misiones District, where families rely on the land to feed themselves through cattle ranching and cotton production, the people are idolising one of their own.

    Diego Gomez’s ascent from the humble beginnings of a farmer’s son to the heart of a Premier League title race is a Hollywood director’s dream. While it is a script that has been read many times before, like an old movie or a classic song, it is also one that never gets old.

    Industry observers note that in this particular iteration, it begins on the dirt tracks of Mburika Reta, which literally translates to the ‘land of donkeys’ in Paraguay’s native Guarani, before winding through the country's capital, Asuncion, and briefly stopping among the palm-lined suburbs of Miami alongside Sergio Busquets and Lionel Messi. It is now gathering pace on England’s south coast, where Brighton find themselves in the unfamiliar territory of hunting down the Premier League champions.

    Gomez is the epitome of Fabian Hurzeler’s machine: energetic, aggressive and relentlessly forward-thinking. It is through this collective sense of selflessness that the Seagulls are second in the table, having already defeated both league leaders Arsenal and Manchester City this season. And for Hurzeler’s versatile midfielder, every performance and goal is a reminder of the moments that forged him.

    ‘He always told me to play forward and, when I have the ball, to have no fear,’ the 23-year-old mentioned last year of his former team-mate Messi.

    Cue a spectacular goal from the halfway line against Crystal Palace last month, the Amex crowd growing feverish as the ball sailed over Walter Benitez before crashing into the back of the net.

    Diego Gomez pictured as a young teen playing for Libertad (left), is now thriving for Paraguay (right) and one of Brighton's most vital players.

    Gomez is congratulated by Pascal Gross after scoring a brilliant goal against Brentford.

    Another quickly followed against Brentford last weekend, with Gomez barely bringing the ball under control before hooking it into the net from 25 yards out with his supposedly weaker left foot, leaving half of his team-mates clutching their heads in disbelief.

    It has been revealed that inevitably Gomez’s rise has not been without its setbacks. It was his mistimed tackle on Desire Doue, stretching out a leg to topple the French winger in the penalty area, that led to the heartache of Paraguay’s World Cup elimination this summer, after Kylian Mbappe slotted home the resulting spot-kick.

    Yet rather than be defined by this mistake, Gomez returned home to a hero’s welcome, mobbed by locals as he was paraded through the streets of the usually sleepy San Juan Bautista in an open-top car.

    It has been revealed that ‘He has the right attitude towards football,’ Hurzeler mentioned shortly after his arrival. ‘He loves to play. You can feel his passion in every talk with him.’.

    Sources indicate that across his 10 appearances this season, Gomez has won 66 duels, more than any Brighton player. His 35 aerial duels won, second behind only Croatian centre back Luka Vuskovic, point to his impressive spring, and he has won 10 tackles, again more than any other Brighton player.

    At the other end of the pitch, meanwhile, he has taken the most touches in the opposition box and has scored two goals and recorded two assists this season.

    While Gomez’s physique gives the impression of a battering ram, he is surprisingly speedy, recording Brighton’s fastest top speed of the season against Chelsea at 21.01mph.

    But who is this kid who was plucked out of nowhere? Who, at the age of 13, moved four hours away from his rural village to the capital to play football, navigating the bus networks as a child to get to training at FC Libertad before a move to join David Beckham’s glitzy side arrived seven years later?

    Gomez, seen with his partner Geraldine Villagra, has taken an unusual route to the top.

    Sources indicate that in this case, it was Inter Miami who did the plucking, with Gomez identified by Brighton’s scouting network while he was playing in the MLS in 2024. Gomez formally joined the club as a 21-year-old in a deal worth £11million in January 2025, having agreed the move six months earlier.

    According to recent reports, former Brighton centre back Gordon Greer is now the club’s pathway development manager and spoke regularly to Gomez during this time, travelling to Florida to see him during the latter stages of the MLS season. It’s fair to say he liked what he found.

    In a recent development, ‘We knew that he would do well because of his application,’ Greer says. ‘He was just a really talented, young, hungry footballer. You could see that he had raw potential, and I think Brighton do that really well. They sign players who have got room to improve.

    ‘The one thing about Diego that is really impressive is his attitude, his work rate. He’s a really driven character and he’s such a humble kid. You can ask Diego to do certain things and he’ll give it his all, no matter what you ask him to do, whether he’s good at it or not. As a coach, it must be amazing to have someone like that in your team.’.

    Sources indicate that during his six-month wait for the move, Gomez undertook regular English lessons, tuned in to Brighton’s games on television and spoke to Hurzeler about the areas he could improve before making the switch. All of that left him with a couple of weeks’ head start, which in Premier League terms is massive.

    Meanwhile, Brighton’s plethora of South American footballers at the time, most notably Julio Enciso, who played alongside him at Libertad, helped him settle quickly. So too did Gomez’s girlfriend, Geraldine Villagra, who moved to Brighton to live with him, while his family regularly visit from Paraguay.

    Gomez is the epitome of Fabian Hurzeler’s energetic machine for the Seagulls.

    Spending 18 months alongside Messi, Busquets and Luis Suarez was also another important step in Gomez’s development, despite his understandable initial nerves. He forged a strong understanding with Messi on the pitch and was the engine that enabled the Argentine genius to thrive. Much like at Brighton, though, that did not stop Gomez from producing moments of magic of his own.

    ‘The fact that he had these superstars in the team probably helped him,’ Greer claims. ‘We don’t have any superstars in our team like Messi, but everyone gives their all.

    ‘At Inter Miami, Messi was by far the best player, but Diego did a lot of the running for him and had a fantastic season in which he contributed a number of goals and assists. He just worked away at it. Regardless of the kind of environment you put him in, he finds a way through it.’.

    Recent findings suggest that the audacity of Gomez’s two recent goals, the strike against Palace that inevitably won the Premier League Goal of the Month award for October and the Brentford one which is firmly in contention for November, almost contradicts that industrious nature. Has Greer been surprised by them?

    Sources indicate that ‘He scored some really good goals for Inter Miami, but not as good as the ones he’s scored of late for us,’ he says. ‘He wants to achieve major things. It’s no surprise... well, it is a surprise when you see him stick one in the top corner with his left foot!’.

    Gomez endeared himself to many when he broke down during a pre-World Cup press conference while speaking about the privilege of representing his country, and he remains deeply aware of where he has come from.

    Earlier this year, Brighton chose to extend their UNICEF partnership to Paraguay, with Gomez becoming an ambassador for a programme that aims to develop young people's skills and confidence through sport and will reach thousands of children across the nation, a role he regards as a great honour.

    After Paraguay’s elimination from the World Cup, Gomez attended one of the events in Asuncion, where he first plied his trade and where UNICEF will soon roll out the programme.

    ‘During his personal time, after coming back from the World Cup, he could have done lots of other things and chose instead to do that,’ Anna Easthope, Brighton’s head of marketing, adds. ‘He realises the impact of meeting kids, giving them inspiration and letting them know that sport is for everyone.’.

    If a hero’s welcome followed World Cup elimination, imagine the reception a Premier League title would bring to Misiones.

    Rob Manfred 'can't imagine' MLB team owners will accept new CBA without a salary cap

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (487 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that major League Baseball commissioner Rob Manfred on Wednesday remarked club owners are not willing to compromise on their push for a salary cap and floor in their ongoing negotiations with the players union on a new collective bargaining agreement.
    • "I can't imagine the owners ratifying a deal that does not include a cap and floor," Manfred stated while meeting with the press during the ongoing owners meetings in Newly introduced York, via the Athletic.
    • Recent findings suggest that "Thirty clubs are 100% unanimous in support of the proposals that have been made," Manfred mentioned later during a news conference at MLB headquarters.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that major League Baseball commissioner Rob Manfred on Wednesday remarked club owners are not willing to compromise on their push for a salary cap and floor in their ongoing negotiations with the players union on a new collective bargaining agreement. While Manfred noted there was general room for compromise with the MLBPA, that does not extend to the central matter of the capped system owners want.

    "I can't imagine the owners ratifying a deal that does not include a cap and floor," Manfred stated while meeting with the press during the ongoing owners meetings in Newly introduced York, via the Athletic.

    Recent findings suggest that "Thirty clubs are 100% unanimous in support of the proposals that have been made," Manfred mentioned later during a news conference at MLB headquarters. "I'm not in a position to speculate about what happens in the event that we don't achieve our overriding objective, which is to get a cap and floor system that addresses the competitive problem that our fans perceive.".

    It has been revealed that it's possible to parse "can't imagine" as a subtle rhetorical hedge. Additionally, Manfred before he was commissioner was the league's lead negotiator. As such, he's quite familiar with the appearance of unyielding resolve as a tactical implement. Thus, the league has tied every other proposed change to the players' acceptance of a cap and floor, and the players through their union have historically shown zero willingness to accept such a system.

    "There can be no clearer example of the league's lack of seriousness than their insistence that they will not negotiate over the economics outside of a radical change to the system that would dramatically reduce overall player compensation for all categories of players and strip fundamental rights from players like the ability to have truly guaranteed contracts," MLBPA interim head Bruce Meyer said Wednesday in a statement.

    Sources indicate that "There should be no illusions about the owners' true motivation in pushing for this system. They want to make more money in profits and franchise values by artificially suppressing player salaries.".

    In their most recent substantive proposal to the players, MLB pitched a $258.3 million cap and $180.2 million floor on team payrolls, with those limits to be phased in gradually. Back in June, the league proposed a $245.3 million cap and $171.2 million floor.

    According to recent reports, the current CBA, which is the accord that governs every aspect of the working relationship between players and clubs in MLB, is set to expire just before midnight on Dec. 1. At that point, the league is expected to lock out the players at the behest of team owners. The lockout will likely not end until a latest CBA is agreed to, at least in principle. Owners also locked out the players in 2021, and that lockout lasted 99 days and very nearly ate into the 2022 regular-season schedule.

    Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • This was the definition of a hard-earned point.
    • Sources indicate that newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight.
    • Sources indicate that even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    This was the definition of a hard-earned point. Newcastle United came back from two goals down to rescue a point against Bournemouth, but this was not a convincing performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side.

    Sources indicate that newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight. It was disjointed and lacklustre as Bournemouth dominated before the break and regularly threatened Lukasz Hornicek in goal.

    Sources indicate that even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination. Whether you believe Harvey Barnes’ wonder goal and Jacob Ramsey’s late strike paper over the cracks or reveal a togetherness – a grit and determination that bodes well for the future – depends on the individual.

    Industry observers note that ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4.

    It has been revealed that for the second weekend in a row, Newcastle had just two shots on target and scored two goals. At the other end of the pitch, they have allowed their opponents 61 shots in just three games, the highest in the division. That is not going to be sustainable long term. Something Jaissle acknowledged.

    It has been revealed that “It highlights where we have potential,” he said. “There are elements to improve offensively.

    “The learning curve is there. There were some elements missing from our performance but there was a strong response. The lads demonstrated substantial character, big personality and big commitment... It is always better to get a point and see the potential to improve.”.

    Sources indicate that A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

    But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

    Industry observers note that in truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

    It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

    When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

    It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

    That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

    On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

    Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

    According to recent reports, tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj.

    Marco Rose’s side should have scored again minutes later when Sven Botman gifted the ball to Evanilson on the edge of the Newcastle area, but he failed to hit the target.

    Bournemouth had their tails up and when another blunder from Dedic – galloping forward and losing possession with a heavy touch – Nico González, another latest signing, failed to make a tackle to stop the attack.

    According to recent reports, justin Kluivert’s long-range strike thumped against the post and hit the back of goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek. Scott reacted quickest and his cross spun into his own net off the leg of Malick Thiaw.

    According to recent reports, bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39.

    Newcastle were in disarray and were lucky to be back in the game before half-time as Barnes whipped in a stunning strike 25 seconds after the restart.

    It has been revealed that bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39.

    Despite seeing more of the ball, other than a Joe Willock header that dropped wide of the post early in the second half, Newcastle did not create another clear goal-scoring opportunity until Ramsey’s equaliser.

    It has been revealed that that is a cause for concern, but Newcastle remain unbeaten. Nothing shapes perceptions more than results. Jaissle is right to cling to the positives from that.

    Speaking to TNT Sports, the Newcastle boss stated: “Mixed feelings. Happy for that spirit, that belief the lads were showing until the end together with the crowd. I felt the energy and felt if we had five or 10 minutes more we could win this game. But the first half was not expected. This is something we need to improve. This is part of the journey.

    Industry observers note that “We knew Bournemouth would come with everything, they always show great intensity and if you do not compete with that you get problems. We struggled with that in the first half but the lads showed the right reaction.”.

    "I'm really happy with the confidence the lads brought onto the pitch today." 👏Marco Rose reflects on Bournemouth's performance after taking a point at St James' Park.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GULqEAUSbx.

    Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday lunchtime fixture between Newcastle United and Bournemouth at St James’ Park.

    The hosts have made a determined start to the 2025-26 season under new head coach Matthias Jaissle. They conceded a last-minute penalty to draw 2-2 with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign, sealed a hard-fought 3-2 victory over West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, and then produced an inspired second-half performance to win 2-0 away at Tottenham in their previous top-flight outing.

    It has been revealed that despite anxiety in the summer after losing Eddie Howe and multiple key players such as Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon, the Jaissle era has begun very encouragingly. Upcoming signings including Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez have seamlessly slotted into the starting XI, Lewis Hall has been typically brilliant, while Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look reborn up top after both forwards endured difficult campaigns last season.

    According to recent reports, marco Rose’s Bournemouth tenure has started in frustrating circumstances. They had been leading 1-0 against Manchester City in their first top-flight fixture this campaign, but conceded two late goals to dramatically lose 2-1. Bournemouth were also left kicking themselves last weekend against Everton, after a defensive mix-up between Ryan Christie and Marcus Tavernier following a corner delivery gifted James Tarkowski a 91st-minute equaliser, allowing the visitors to salvage a 1-1 draw at the Vitality Stadium.

    Sources indicate that at opposite ends of the country, over 350 miles separate these two sides. Away days in English football can’t really get any longer. The travelling Bournemouth support will hope their loyalty can be repaid with a first Premier League win of the season under Rose, while Newcastle will aim to continue their unbeaten start and carry on the positive momentum created by Jaissle.

    Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

    Week 12 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Can the Seahawks, or anyone, stop the 49ers?

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1539 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, last season, the San Francisco 49ers won a close game at the Seattle Seahawks.
    • We have the 49ers' road win over the Seahawks out of the way already this season.
    • In a recent development, the 49ers have been great this season, including a dominant win over the Minnesota Vikings last week.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, last season, the San Francisco 49ers won a close game at the Seattle Seahawks. And then after that the Seahawks became a dominant Super Bowl champion, including two blowout wins of the 49ers.

    We have the 49ers' road win over the Seahawks out of the way already this season. But this season San Francisco is the team that looks like a future Super Bowl champion.

    In a recent development, the 49ers have been great this season, including a dominant win over the Minnesota Vikings last week. The offense has been spectacular. And the defense, ranked seventh in DVOA, has been one of the biggest surprises of the season. That defense has brought the 49ers from being a good team to a potentially great one. Kyle Shanahan, who should be NFL Coach of the Year, was going to field a potent offense. The defense completes the circle.

    However, we can't count out the Seahawks quite yet. The defense has been tremendous again. The offense hasn't been great, but a lot of that is attributed to Sam Darnold playing through injuries almost all season, when he has been able to play. Darnold should return this week, off the Seahawks' bye, and if he's a little healthier and a bit more protective of the ball, Seattle can still play at a high level.

    According to recent reports, that's why the Seahawks are not a big underdog this week, even though they play at a 9-1 49ers team. The 49ers are just a 3-point favorite. Not setting the spread above a field goal highlights a lot of respect for the reigning champions. But maybe it's not showing enough respect for the 49ers.

    San Francisco has shown no signs of vulnerability. It had no issues with the Vikings defense, which is the only defense on the same level as Seattle. This looks like a great San Francisco team, and that's why 49ers -3 is the pick. And if the Seahawks can't slow down the 49ers, nobody else in the NFC might be able to do it either.

    Industry observers note that brock Purdy and the San Francisco 49ers beat the Seahawks 32-29 back in Week 5. (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images).

    Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 12 of the NFL season:.

    The Rams might be in some trouble without Puka Nacua, but they're not a bad team. Especially on defense. It is going to be hard for the Packers to move the ball. They aren't running the ball against the defense that ranks No. 1 in DVOA against the run. They will try to throw it downfield to Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, but that requires the offensive line holding up and that could be a problem against the Rams' line. Perhaps the Rams' offense struggles, but it seems like they can grind out a win.

    It's a little surprising to see Detroit as this major of an underdog. The Lions are 8-2 and very good, especially with the recent defensive improvement. But that defense hasn't faced an offense like Chicago's in a while. The Bears are cooking on offense and defense lately. They haven't even trailed in a game in five weeks. Detroit's defense has been good lately but at some point it seems like injuries to linebacker Jack Campbell and defensive end Aidan Hutchinson will catch up to them, and it could be this week.

    The one dud among the five games between Wednesday and Friday. Here's the conundrum: You can't trust the Cowboys defense to help cover a substantial spread (even though it did look a little better last week), but you also can't really trust Joe Milton III to help keep the game close. Hopefully the Eagles will be up to playing spoiler for a large audience.

    The biggest factor in this game is whether Buffalo's defensive improvement — the Bills have allowed 37 points in four games — can stick or if it's due to facing a run of bad quarterbacks. If the defensive improvement is legitimate, Buffalo might have its best team of the Josh Allen era. We should find out this week. The Chiefs are very good, too, and in a great matchup it seems smart to grab the three points, though we'll want to confirm that Kenneth Walker III is back from injury for this one.

    Benching Aaron Rodgers wasn't outlandish after two bad games and a pretty mediocre season. But the way it played out, with it being announced after 11 p.m. on a Tuesday when the Steelers play Friday, was stunning. Now we have to figure out if the Steelers will revolt or rally around Mason Rudolph. This one could get weird, in what is supposed to be rainy weather. The Broncos seem to have found their offensive identity through rookie running back Jonah Coleman, but the Steelers are very good stopping the run. Pittsburgh also should get back to its run game after inexplicably forgetting about it last week, which means Rudolph won't be much of a factor anyway. This has already been a weird week in Pittsburgh.

    PHILADELPHIA, PA - NOVEMBER 22: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers looks on during the game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Pittsburgh Steelers on Nov. 22, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA.

    It has been revealed that the Bengals should be upset after losing in the final seconds at Washington on Monday night. And they can take it out on the Saints, who have lost three of four with the only win being when they held off an overtime two-point conversation at home against Shedeur Sanders and the Browns. Joe Burrow should have another monster game.

    It has been revealed that kyle McCord was reasonable in his first start, but that was against the Colts. Last week at Buffalo the Dolphins had what was probably their worst game of the season, and that's saying something for a 1-9 team. The Jets aren't good, but they are coming off a win over the Chargers, and they'll look better when they're playing teams down at their level.

    In a recent development, the worst thing to happen to Jesse Minter is the defense struggling as badly as it has. If the Ravens were losing because the offense was inept without Lamar Jackson, it would be easy to give him a pass. But Jacoby Brissett has been reasonable and the defense, which is Minter's specialty, has been awful. Baltimore has allowed 32.4 points per game over the past five weeks. The Texans can move the ball and now see an opening for a wild-card spot with the upheaval in Pittsburgh.

    It's hard to take any underdog lately, with the favorites on a roll the past few weeks. And the Falcons aren't a comfortable underdog to take, but Atlanta has enough talent that it's still the only team to beat the 49ers. The Falcons are coming off a bye, and maybe that helps them keep it close.

    It has been revealed that switching quarterbacks can give a team a short-term boost, especially when that quarterback was the worst in the NFL this season. Daniel Jones wasn't giving the Colts a chance. Anthony Richardson Sr. hasn't been good in the NFL, but he can't be worse than Jones has been. Maybe there's a jolt that gives Indianapolis a chance to keep this one close.

    It would have been nice to see the Titans play better at Dallas last week, but they did end up scoring 30 points. The offense has been decent lately. The problem is the defense, and that's why it's scary to take them even getting more than two touchdowns. But that's a major spread in the NFL.

    In a recent development, this game could be Tommy DeVito vs. D.J. Uiagalelei, if Justin Herbert doesn't clear concussion protocol. Since there's no reason to rush Herbert back we'll assume he won't play, and then this could turn into one of the ugliest games in the NFL this season.

    According to recent reports, the Cardinals have shown no signs of life lately, after trading Jacoby Brissett, watching Gardner Minshew II go down to injury, losing all their receivers due to injury or trades and then firing their defensive coordinator this week. Whether rookie Carson Beck returns from a back injury or Josh Johnson has to start again, it doesn't really matter. The Commanders aren't great but we can't trust Arizona.

    According to recent reports, fernando Mendoza didn't look bad last week. The Raiders' defense is still terrible and maybe the Browns break out against it, but Cleveland's offense has its issues too. The Browns play close games, that's what they do, and we'll assume another close one on Sunday night.

    Tampa Bay is getting very little out of Baker Mayfield. But the Buccaneers can still run the ball and play very good defense. A win for Tampa Bay would still leave them at 4-7, but they'd be just a game behind the Panthers for first place and clinch the head-to-head tiebreaker. The first meeting was an absolute blowout, and while that won't repeat, it showed that Tampa Bay is a hard matchup for Carolina.

    Breaking: MLB rumors: Mets to meet with NPB star, plus latest on Ketel Marte, Cubs, Mariners, Nationals, more

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1235 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We're one week away from Thanksgiving and the offseason has started to pick up a little bit in Major League Baseball.
    • We can hold out hope, as there has been enough movement to keep belief alive.
    • It has been revealed that it's no secret that the Diamondbacks are willing to trade All-Star second baseman Ketel Marte.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We're one week away from Thanksgiving and the offseason has started to pick up a little bit in Major League Baseball. We've seen an All-Star pitcher sign (Sonny Gray to the Twins) and a trade involving an All-Star (Maikel Garcia to the Mariners). The White Sox also signed a mid-rotation starter while the Red Sox grabbed a first baseman fresh off a World Series title. Is there enough time for a flurry of moves before the owners lock the players out when the CBA expires on Dec. 1?

    In theory, there sure is. We can hold out hope, as there has been enough movement to keep belief alive.

    It has been revealed that it's no secret that the Diamondbacks are willing to trade All-Star second baseman Ketel Marte. A massive hurdle might be his 10-and-5 no-trade rights and questions about which teams Marte would approve in a potential deal. Further, the asking price on Arizona's end is "very high," reports FanSided. Still, plenty of teams are noted to be interested.

    Marte, 33, has five years and $91.75 million left on his deal. He finished third in MVP voting in 2024, was a highly productive All-Star in 2025, but some problems arose in 2026, including several no-shows. He hit .249/.316/.432 (107 OPS+) with 2.5 WAR and some possible clubhouse baggage.

    In a recent development, the Mets are planning a Zoom meeting with Japanese right-hander Kaima Taira, reports the Upcoming York Post. This won't have an impact on their pursuit of Tarik Skubal, just in case anyone is curious.

    It has been revealed that taira, 27, has been one of the top pitchers in Japan's NPB for years. Last season, in 23 starts, he had a 1.36 ERA and 0.96 WHIP with 141 strikeouts in 146 innings. He's had a sub-2.00 ERA four of the last five seasons, with the exception being a 2.40 in 2023.

    In a recent development, CBS Sports ranked Taira as the No. 19 free agent available this winter:.

    Industry observers note that listed at 5-foot-8, Taira gets outlier extension down the mound (close to seven feet despite his height), which creates a low release window. Hitters rarely see the ball come from where Taira releases it. He's not a gimmick pitcher either. Taira sits mid-90s with his four-seam fastball and backs it up with a cutter, sinker, sweeper, slider, changeup, and splitter. The sweeper and slider are distinct pitches, as are the changeup and splitter. The Seibu Lions used Taira as a reliever in 2024 and 2025, then started him in 2026, and he handled the assignment well. The breaking balls are just OK, and the fact of the matter is that pitchers this height don't often hold up under a starter's workload. I would assume the team that signs Taira will give him a chance to start. In the long run, though, he might be a reliever, perhaps even a multi-inning setup man. Seibu announced on Oct. 30 that Taira will be posted this offseason.

    Because of the expected lockout, international free agents are working under an artificial Dec. 1 deadline to sign, rather than the normal posting window.

    For now, the Mets' rotation starts with Nolan McLean and Christian Scott.

    According to recent reports, the Cubs' main focus is on pitching, as well it should be after having one of the worst pitching staffs in baseball along with one of the best collections of position-player talent. Still, both corner outfielders (Ian Happ and Seiya Suzuki) have hit free agency along with catcher Carson Kelly, so they can't just ignore the offense. On that front, the ballclub has "extensively scouted" Teruaki Sato, according to The Athletic.

    Sato has played mostly third base, where the Cubs have Alex Bregman, but also has outfield experience and could simply serve as DH. In 143 games last season in NPB, Sato hit .306/.383/.609 with 40 doubles, 39 home runs and 106 RBI. His strikeout numbers are high, but sometimes that's the price to be paid for top-level power.

    In a recent development, CBS Sports ranked Sato as the No. 4 free agent this winter:.

    Sources indicate that he will play the entire 2027 season at age 28 and is coming off a .306/.383/.609 slash line with 39 home runs, which won him Japan's first Triple Crown since Munetaka Murakami in 2022. Sato has a similar skill set but is not quite Murakami 2.0. He doesn't have quite as much power (but has plenty of it) and won't walk nearly as often, but he does swing and miss a bunch and is unlikely to remain at the hot corner long-term. Sato is a very aggressive hitter who ran a 66% contact rate this past season. That is below the 77% MLB average. The consensus seems to be that he will land at first base or in a corner outfield spot if not next year, then soon. Murakami successfully overcame his contact problems to slug 35 homers in only 127 games around a hamstring injury. At minimum, that will have MLB teams reconsidering how they evaluate the Japan-to-MLB transition. Like Murakami, Sato carries risk, and like Murakami, his power makes that risk worth the dice roll.

    According to recent reports, after being one of the most disappointing teams in 2026 and having an active general manager, of course the Mariners weren't going to just sit around after one move. Sure enough, Jerry Dipoto told reporters on Wednesday that they are still looking to add a right-handed bat (remember, Randy Arozarena is a free agent) along with a veteran infielder and a left-handed reliever even after acquiring Garcia. And perhaps most importantly, Dipoto insisted that they do have the payroll flexibility to add all of this.

    Further, he also mentioned the rotation is set and no other starting pitchers will be moved. So it'll be Logan Gilbert, George Kirby, Bryan Woo, Emerson Hancock and Kade Anderson heading into next season.

    Fresh off signing right-handed starter Dustin May, the White Sox are looking to add another starting pitcher "of similar magnitude," reports the Chicago Sun-Times.

    Recent findings suggest that though the White Sox were one of baseball's best stories last season and made the playoffs, the rotation was very thin. Right now, they have Sean Burke, May, Taylor, Davis Martin and Anthony Kay as their top five and are looking to add another of May's ilk. Things are already looking much better.

    In a recent development, the Nationals finished third in the majors in runs scored last season, believe it or not. They trailed only the Cubs and Brewers, scoring more than the Dodgers. The problem was that the pitching staff was mostly a mess. As such, it's no surprise they are after starters and The Athletic names three targets: lefty Kris Bubic, righty Brady Singer and Japanese import Kona Takahashi.

    Sources indicate that bubic, 29, has battled shoulder and elbow injuries the past two seasons, but the upside was flashed in the first part of 2025. He made the All-Star team and had a 2.55 ERA through 20 starts and 116 ⅓ innings.

    The 30-year-old Singer was 6-15 with a 5.85 ERA for the Reds last season in a disaster of a contract year, but he was productive in the previous two seasons.

    Takahashi, 29, was 9-7 with a 2.64 ERA, 1.10 WHIP and 118 strikeouts in 143 ⅓ innings in NPB last season.

    #119953. Luis Castillo trade grades: White Sox give up steady back-end starter to offload salary; Rockies get creative

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (686 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Luis Castillo trade grades: White Sox give up steady back-end starter to offload salary; Rockies get creative

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (686 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, two days after adding Dustin May to their rotation, the Chicago White Sox have subtracted Luis Castillo and Davis Martin.
    • Sources indicate that castillo, 33, joined the White Sox in a deadline trade with the Seattle Mariners.
    • It has been revealed that the 29-year-old Martin threw 146 innings with a 3.95 ERA in 2026, but it was a 3.41 ERA in the first half and a 5.12 ERA in the second half.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, two days after adding Dustin May to their rotation, the Chicago White Sox have subtracted Luis Castillo and Davis Martin. The White Sox are sending Castillo and Martin to the Colorado Rockies for lefty Sean Sullivan and minor-league catcher Douglas Veliz, the teams announced late Thursday. The Rockies will take on Castillo's entire contract.

    Sources indicate that castillo, 33, joined the White Sox in a deadline trade with the Seattle Mariners. He struggled badly after the deal, allowing 30 runs in 31 innings, and he finished the season on the injured list with a shoulder problem. Castillo has one year remaining on his contract at $22.75 million, though a $25 million option for 2028 will vest if he throws 150 innings in 2027.

    It has been revealed that the 29-year-old Martin threw 146 innings with a 3.95 ERA in 2026, but it was a 3.41 ERA in the first half and a 5.12 ERA in the second half. The White Sox kept him at arm's length in the postseason despite running bullpen games almost nightly. Martin allowed two runs in one inning in his only postseason appearance.

    According to recent reports, neither Sullivan nor Veliz are significant prospects. For all intents and purposes, the White Sox are attaching Martin to Castillo as a sweetener to get the Rockies to take Castillo's salary. The Rockies are essentially buying Martin, who is under team control through 2030, by taking on the rest of Castillo's contract.

    Here now are our trade grades for this two-for-two swap.

    Sources indicate that fair or not, I'm going to lump the two Castillo trades together. Chicago stepped out to acquire Castillo at the deadline and absorbed the $30 million or so remaining on his contract to do it. Seranthony Domínguez, who had about $15 million left on his deal, went the other way in the trade, so the White Sox took on about $15 million total, and also gave up a pretty good prospect in Boston Smith.

    Four and a half months later, the White Sox had to give up a steady back-end starter in Martin to clear Castillo's money. They ended up saving about $7 million in 2027 in this series of moves, but it cost them Martin and Smith (and Domínguez), and they had to endure 31 awful innings from Castillo. Unless Sullivan or Veliz hit massive, the White Sox took a series of Ls here.

    Credit to president of baseball operations Chris Getz for acknowledging a mistake with Castillo and acting rapidly to unload him. It was costly, though. Martin isn't a star, but cheap back-end starters are very valuable. We'll see what Getz & Co. do with the savings. Presumably they'll invest in more pitching. Having to give up Martin to dump Castillo so soon is a stinker, though. Ouch.

    Sources indicate that the Rockies need all types of pitching (righty, lefty, starter, reliever, whatever) and it's not often they can convince quality (or even competent) free agents to come to Coors Field. They have to develop their own pitchers or trade for pitching, and in this instance, they took on Castillo's hefty salary to get Martin and his four years of control. Creative, if nothing else.

    Industry observers note that there is downside potential too. Martin has run below league-average strikeout rates and middling ground ball rates throughout his career. Pitchers who allow a lot of balls in play -- a lot of balls in play in the air -- are a poor match for Coors Field. It's good the Rockies spent and found a way to add controllable pitching. They just might not have picked the best pitcher.

    It has been revealed that after losing 104 games in 2026, there is no such thing as a bad dart throw for the Rockies. It's unlikely they would have been able to spend the $22.75 million on a free agent (at least not without overpaying), so taking on Castillo to get Martin is the next best thing. I like the thinking, even if I don't love Martin's profile in Coors Field.

    Industry News: What's next for the Twins? Three things Minnesota must do to make a postseason push in 2027 season

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1101 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
